premise.zh: 现代都市里的魔法战争：十二件遗器，十二个持有者，谁先握住五件谁就能改写世界的一条规则。每一次全力出手都要付一段记忆。好玩在“赢下来的那个人，还记不记得自己为什么要赢”。
premise.en: A modern-city magic war: twelve relics, twelve holders, and whoever holds five may rewrite one rule of the world. Every all-out use costs a memory. The fun is whether the one who wins still remembers why they wanted to.

power.zh: 力量：读懂对手、看清结构攒下来的余裕。靠它出手能少付代价；结局不能只看它。
power.en: Power: the margin earned by reading opponents and structures. It lets you pay less; an ending never rests on it alone.

memory.zh: 记忆：主角还剩下的回忆。全力出手就要交出一段，交出去的拿不回来，后面的选项和台词跟着变。
memory.en: Memory: what the protagonist still remembers. Going all out gives one up for good, and later choices and lines change with it.

risk.zh: 注意：守秘局和对手对你的注意。到线必须出事（上门盘问、被盯上），不能只是一个数字。
risk.en: Notice: how closely the Secrecy Bureau and rivals are watching. Crossing the line must cause something (a visit, a tail), not just change a number.

failures.zh: 空壳：交出去的记忆太多，赢了也想不起为什么要赢
failures.en: Hollow: so many memories given up that winning means nothing

failures.zh: 读错招：对手的意图看错了，代价来不及付
failures.en: Misread: the opponent's intent was wrong and the price comes too late

failures.zh: 暴露：在普通人面前用了遗器，守秘局先动手
failures.en: Exposed: a relic used before ordinary people, and the Bureau moves first

checklist.zh: 魔法是剧情规则，代价写清楚：拿走什么、拿不拿得回来
checklist.en: Magic is a story rule; its price is explicit: what is taken, and whether it comes back

checklist.zh: 坏结局要能学到东西：每个坏结局后给出回到哪一步、为什么
checklist.en: A bad ending teaches: each one says which step to revisit, and why

checklist.zh: 全力出手总有一个不全力的走法，只是更难、更慢，或者要先看懂结构
checklist.en: Every all-out moment has a way that isn't, only harder, slower, or needing the structure read first
